scope: Local code, isolated PostgreSQL and loopback HTTP only. No production/staging, schema/index/pool changes, backup work or retention policy/application.

verifiedCostSources: raw role/profile rows; independent resolvers rebuilt per request
Omie category filters with their full options
guards: pending sources coalesce only for the same version/key
Dates, Maps, precision and internal aliases retained in independent V8 snapshots
changes.cards: The authenticated cards route enters the same verified response cache as detail/group/point. User and financial projection remain in the DTO key. Legacy intermediate card/dashboard/labor caches receive the verified version, so external writes can be observed without clearing API memory.
changes.defaultFlag: ACOMPANHAMENTO_READ_CACHE_ENABLED=false; no new flag or migration
changes.queriesAndRules: Existing catalog and report queries/ordering are unchanged. No JSONB metadata packet or RDO tie rule was integrated.

validation.notes: The full 30-test PostgreSQL batch covers CRM/presentations with caching enabled. After refining the synthetic worker to edit RDO minutes, the 9 relevant HTTP/group/catalog contracts were rerun. Application source stayed unchanged during that refinement; final 17 fingerprints preceded final parity/measurements.

statesCovered: effective salary parameters written through an independent pg connection
annual costs and category changes committed by an independent transaction
catalogHttpParity.reference: A fresh API process without verified caching per state. Candidate API remains alive without memory clears after external writes. Reusing the unversioned API would leave its legacy TTL caches in the reference.
catalogHttpParity.revisionFailure: Cached cards reject a failed revision check with 503. A new catalog load failure preserves the existing detail error contract, does not fall back to a preceding revision, and retries on the next request.

validation.workflowYaml: parsed and verified cards/CRM/presentation gate present

normalization: monthly report generatedAt emission time only
parity.method: Separate control/candidate processes on the same database. Each surface has a GET context and real databaseReadVersion; per-process catalogs/monthly snapshots are exercised across surfaces. Maps/Sets retain entry order in the digest. No financial value, allocation trail, CNPJ, date or revision token is removed.

httpMethod.method: Synthetic loopback HTTP against the real Express app and migrated PostgreSQL. Authentication validates persisted hashed sessions through requireAuth; password login is not exercised. First-process samples use a fresh API process per request, with warm database pages and process imports excluded. Warm requests mix surfaces, profiles and two sessions per profile under a bounded shared concurrency. Client timing includes response-body receipt; server timing includes authentication and serialization. Active-pool interval samples are observations, not individual query wait times. No Nginx, TLS, browser rendering, external API or production load is measured.
httpMethod.database: PostgreSQL 16, CPU=1, memory=768 MiB, loopback only; 250 migrations
httpMethod.worker: Independent API/controller clients. The controller changes realized service measurements, increments one RDO daytimeWorkedMinutes by 60, changes point minutes and adds an unmatched summary. Project.updatedAt must remain unchanged. No API memory invalidation.
httpMethod.cardRefreshOracle: Match projectId, groupId and id; compare workedHours.normalWorkedHours. A point change alone can leave a dense card monetary total unchanged; monetary difference is not a general freshness oracle.
httpMethod.baselineLimitation: The old cards route retains its unversioned TTL result after the commit. Baselines record cards.changed=false and refreshWithin15s=false; legacy baselines are retained rather than aborted. The candidate integration test requires all four surfaces to refresh.

httpConclusion.limits: Global pool target remains open. Warm SQL is lower, but post-write SQL/latency cannot be presented as a uniform performance win: the candidate now refreshes the cards while the baseline serves the preceding card values. One write event and one cold response per route/profile do not establish cold/post-write p95.

sparse.method: Local paired uncached service calculations on PostgreSQL with warm database pages; not HTTP latency. Timings exclude process boot and module imports. Fresh Node/Prisma processes for every cold sample. After-session performs a SELECT, not HTTP authentication. Prisma operation profiles include mapping; sqlQueries capture pg pool calls and replay SELECTs with EXPLAIN ANALYZE after the calculation. Pool call durations overlap and include queue/event-loop delays. Initialization diagnostics run in separate processes and do not warm timed samples. Result bytes are JSON sizes, not network traffic.
sparse.cpuMethod: process.cpuUsage delta around the calculation only, before EXPLAIN replay; includes Node/Prisma CPU, excludes PostgreSQL, module imports and process boot. CPU and wall time are separate observations.

dense.method: Local paired uncached service calculations on PostgreSQL with warm database pages; not HTTP latency. Timings exclude process boot and module imports. Fresh Node/Prisma processes for every cold sample. After-session performs a SELECT, not HTTP authentication. service.interpretation: Unverified service calculations bypass both monthly and catalog snapshots. These paired cumulative timings measure the whole plan against its original source; they do not isolate or credit this stage with the wall-time variation. Five pairs per mode/case, alternating source order; cold excludes boot/imports and uses warm database pages. Both cold medians remain below the 50% reduction target.

sourceOrderDiagnostic.method: A separate diagnostic preloader observes pg Report SELECT results and retains only SQL/parameter/ordered/unordered hashes and counts. Both source variants are instrumented; this is not latency evidence. The old rejected parallel JSONB metadata preloader was used only in diagnostic children.
sourceOrderDiagnostic.conclusion: All 15 new instrumented pairs were equal; two unordered input groups had no reordered hashes. This does not replace the earlier failed sparse cohort, establish its cause or authorize integrating either metadata-packet prototype.

precedingMeasurements.reason: The first control preceded cards integration. Three later cohorts used a monetary card-delta observation with only point/service edits. Both control and candidate had false observations in the dense fixture; financial totals may legitimately remain equal. No successful cohort was substituted after a latency miss. The final oracle directly edits and verifies RDO hours, with identical final inputs for both sources.

candidate.issue: Both attempts logged Temporary failure resolving for Ubuntu package mirrors. Backend stopped during Hunspell installation before Data Book/backend tests. Frontend passed tests/lint/build/loading budgets, but browser dependency installation repeatedly failed DNS resolution and was cancelled.
candidate.cancellation: The owned attempts were cancelled after the setup stalled; only unsuccessful jobs were retried once. No checks were removed or weakened.
pendingChecks: general backend/Data Book suites in CI
candidate.nextAction: Retry unsuccessful jobs on the same implementation commit after runner DNS recovers. Local source checks and the nine successful jobs remain recorded separately.

limitations: This stage remains opt-in; defaults, pools and business rules are unchanged. The extra catalog budget is bounded in process memory and is not a distributed cache.
No production, browser rendering, TLS/proxy or 24-hour/seven-day acceptance. All figures are synthetic local observations on a shared API host.
No causal cold-speed claim for the verified catalog cache: unverified cold service calculations do not use it. No composing percentages from different rounds.
The rejected metadata transport remains rejected. Original source rows are not reordered or normalized to force RDO evidence parity.
